summary_ja: 事業法人等向けエクスポージャーのPD推計手法とその要件、観測期間を定める。
summary_en: Sets the methods and requirements for estimating PD for corporate, etc. exposures, and the five-year minimum observation period.
paragraphs: An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach shall use one or more of the methods set out in the following items, or other information and methods consistent with long-run experience that are similar to them. In this case, the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach shall estimate the PD of each rating as the average of the one-year default probabilities calculated as a simple average based on the number of obligors, and shall not estimate PD as an exposure-weighted average: (i) a method of estimating, from internal data on actual defaults, the long-run average PD corresponding to the obligor ratings of corporate, etc. exposures; (ii) a method of estimating PD by linking internal ratings with external ratings and assigning to each rating the PD corresponding to the external rating (hereinafter in this Article referred to as "mapping"); (iii) a method of calculating, on the basis of a model, the estimated default probability of each individual obligor belonging to an obligor rating and taking the simple average of those estimates as the PD.

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach uses a method of estimating PD from internal data on actual defaults in estimating the PD of the obligor ratings of corporate, etc. exposures, it shall satisfy the following requirements: (i) the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach shall reflect the differences between the credit extension standards and internal rating system at the time the data was generated and the current internal rating system, and shall describe its analysis of how this is reflected in its credit risk management guidelines; (ii) the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach shall conservatively adjust its PD estimates where the available data is limited or where the credit extension standards or the internal rating system have changed; (iii) where the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach uses data pooled among multiple financial institutions, the internal rating systems and standards of the other financial institutions that contribute data to the pool shall not diverge significantly from the internal rating system and standards of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach.

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach uses mapping in estimating the PD of the obligor ratings of corporate, etc. exposures, it shall satisfy the following requirements: (i) the mapping is based on a comparison of the criteria of internal ratings and external ratings and a comparison of internal ratings and external ratings for common obligors; (ii) the mapping method or the data used for quantification is not biased and is not inconsistent; (iii) the standards of the external credit assessment institution, etc. that underlie the data used for quantification relate to obligor risk and do not take into account characteristics relating to the exposure; (iv) the credit risk management guidelines describe the comparison and analysis of events treated as default under the internal rating criteria and the external rating criteria, and the mapping criteria.

In estimating the PD of corporate, etc. exposures, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach shall use one or more of external data, internal data, or data pooled among multiple financial institutions, covering an observation period of five years or more.

In using the data referred to in the preceding paragraph, the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach shall include in its coverage the data covering the longest observation period, and that data shall include years that represent typical good economic times and years that represent bad economic times; provided, however, that this does not apply to data that has low relevance or is immaterial for estimating PD.
